practices.practice: Maintain detailed build records linking each VIN to its specific components and label values, while keeping warranty claims and dealer reports reviewable.
practices.why_it_matters: Inspection sign-off and label verification are compliance steps, not just quality steps, and keeping warranty claims, complaints, and dealer reports reviewable ensures regulatory compliance.
practices.source: NHTSA New Manufacturers Handbook: Requirements for Manufacturers of Motor Vehicles and Motor Vehicle Equipment (revision 10/24/2025)

practices.practice: Use AI to prepare, check compliance paperwork, and flag documentation gaps for certification labels and VIN requirements.
practices.why_it_matters: Manufacturers must self-certify compliance with FMVSS, and errors can trigger civil penalties of up to $27,168 per violation.
practices.source: NHTSA New Manufacturers Handbook: Requirements for Manufacturers of Motor Vehicles and Motor Vehicle Equipment (revision 10/24/2025)

practices.practice: Automate document extraction, matching (invoices to purchase orders to payments), monthly reconciliation, and record retention.
practices.why_it_matters: These tasks are routine, repetitive, and rule-governed, making them ideal for assisted automation with a human approving exceptions.
practices.source: IRS Publication 583 (Rev. December 2024), Starting a Business and Keeping Records

practices.practice: Implement value stream mapping and 5S workplace organization as foundational continuous-improvement steps.
practices.why_it_matters: Value stream mapping exposes waste and shows where to focus, while 5S improves safety and makes maintenance easier without requiring upfront spending.
practices.source: NIST Manufacturing Extension Partnership: Lean and process improvement

practices.practice: Deploy AI tools to spot problems early, analyze business data, automate repeat tasks, and improve customer service.
practices.why_it_matters: Delivers core operational benefits while requiring human oversight to safeguard data, ensure accuracy and ethics, and manage customer expectations.
practices.source: SBA Business Guide: AI for small business

scored_opportunities.name: Quote Spec Validator Agent
scored_opportunities.what_the_agent_does: Parses customer and dealer trailer specifications, cross-references them against manufacturing constraints and pricing tiers, and auto-generates compliant quotes with real-time availability checks.
scored_opportunities.gap: Manual spec verification causes quote turnaround delays and errors in custom options.
scored_opportunities.rating_reason: High value due to direct revenue impact and reduced quote delays; moderate effort requires ERP integration; low risk as it only suggests quotes for human approval.

scored_opportunities.name: Dealer Application Processor Agent
scored_opportunities.what_the_agent_does: Extracts dealer application data, populates financing partner forms, checks credit thresholds, and flags missing documentation for manual review.
scored_opportunities.gap: Manual data entry and financing approval delays slow dealer portal access and order processing.
scored_opportunities.rating_reason: Strong value by accelerating dealer onboarding; moderate effort for lender API integration; medium risk due to financial data handling requiring strict validation.

scored_opportunities.name: Supply Chain Disruption Predictor Agent
scored_opportunities.what_the_agent_does: Monitors supplier lead times for steel and components, predicts delays using historical production data, and suggests alternative sourcing or production schedule adjustments.
scored_opportunities.gap: Reactive supply chain management leads to steel/component delays and labor scheduling conflicts.
scored_opportunities.rating_reason: High value by preventing production stoppages; high effort due to complex supplier data integration; medium risk as incorrect predictions could cause minor schedule shifts.

scored_opportunities.name: VIN-to-Component Warranty Tracker Agent
scored_opportunities.what_the_agent_does: Links each registered trailer’s VIN to its specific build components, auto-verifies warranty eligibility against registration dates, and flags claims for manual review.
scored_opportunities.gap: Manual registration processing and claim verification delays frustrate customers and increase admin overhead.
scored_opportunities.rating_reason: High value improves customer trust and reduces claim fraud; moderate effort requires linking legacy build data to new CRM; low risk as it only flags claims for human verification.

scored_opportunities.name: Inventory Replenishment Optimizer Agent
scored_opportunities.what_the_agent_does: Tracks real-time parts inventory levels, predicts demand based on seasonal sales and warranty claims, and auto-generates purchase orders for critical components.
scored_opportunities.gap: Manual parts inventory tracking leads to stockouts and shipping delays for owners.
scored_opportunities.rating_reason: Solid value by reducing stockouts and shipping delays; moderate effort for WMS integration; medium risk due to potential overstocking if demand forecasts are inaccurate.

scored_opportunities.name: Feedback Data Unification Agent
scored_opportunities.what_the_agent_does: Cleanses and standardizes disparate survey responses, dealer reports, and service logs into a centralized knowledge base for cross-departmental access.
scored_opportunities.gap: Survey data siloing and inconsistent formatting prevent actionable insights.
scored_opportunities.rating_reason: Lower immediate value but critical for enabling future AI agents; moderate effort due to data cleaning complexity; very low risk as it only structures existing data.

roadmaps.rationale: Beginning with unifying customer feedback and service logs establishes a clean, centralized data foundation that reduces errors in downstream quoting and warranty processes. Standardizing this information first minimizes compliance risks and ensures that subsequent automated validators operate on accurate, cross-departmental data. This cautious sequencing aligns with a low-risk tolerance by prioritizing data integrity before automating customer-facing and post-sale operations.
roadmaps.pilot_reason: The Feedback Data Unification Agent is piloted first because it carries the lowest implementation risk and directly improves data quality across departments without disrupting active sales or production workflows.
roadmaps.assumption: Disparate survey responses, dealer reports, and service logs contain sufficiently structured or standardizable fields to be successfully cleansed and merged into a single knowledge base.

roadmaps.rationale: Starting with the lowest-effort website assistant allows the business to capture customer interest and streamline initial inquiries without disrupting core manufacturing operations. Implementing the dealer application processor next leverages existing financing partnerships to accelerate revenue cycles, while the inventory optimizer ensures that parts availability keeps pace with growing sales. This progression delivers immediate operational relief and cash flow improvements while keeping implementation complexity manageable for a risk-averse owner.
roadmaps.pilot_reason: The Website AI assistant is piloted first because it requires minimal integration with internal systems, allowing the business to quickly test customer engagement and handoff protocols before scaling to dealer financing and inventory workflows.
roadmaps.assumption: The approved business information used by the website assistant is consistently updated and accurately reflects current pricing, availability, and dealer networks.

roadmaps.rationale: Establishing a unified feedback and service data foundation first ensures that all subsequent automation tools operate on accurate, standardized information rather than fragmented records. Implementing the quoting validator next builds directly on this clean data to ensure compliance and pricing accuracy, while the website assistant leverages the unified knowledge base to provide reliable customer guidance. This sequence prioritizes structural readiness, ensuring that each subsequent tool has the necessary data infrastructure to function correctly.
roadmaps.pilot_reason: The Feedback Data Unification Agent is piloted first because it creates the essential data backbone required for both quoting accuracy and customer-facing AI responses, making it a true prerequisite for the roadmap's success.
roadmaps.assumption: The business has the internal bandwidth and cross-departmental cooperation to standardize disparate data sources without disrupting daily customer service or sales operations.

rubric.objection: While the enabler approach is sound, placing a website AI assistant after data unification and quoting validation feels slightly out of order; it would be more impactful to integrate the assistant with those systems first.
